purpose: Measure whether the experimental look-ahead opening policy (draft-aware-2026-10-12: both settlements and their starting roads) wins more simulated four-player base games than the classic Catan Lens policy, the bots' own opening and taking the most pips, against Catanatron's value-function bots. No outcome of this run is used to tune anything.

armLabels.lens-draft: Catan Lens look-ahead (experimental) settlements and road
armLabels.lens: Catan Lens classic settlements and road

analysis: Every arm plays the same 8,000 boards and seats: 20 bot tie-breaking seeds (hash seeds 401 to 420) times 400 boards (board seeds 4,000,000 to 4,007,999). Primary: lens-draft minus lens; secondary: lens-draft minus value; descriptive: lens-draft minus pips. Each comparison reports the two-sided approximate 95% Student t interval over the 20 cluster (hash seed) mean differences, df 19, in percentage points, and the exact two-sided McNemar test on the boards whose win or loss changed. Following the rule in results.md, a difference counts as significant only when both agree: the interval excludes zero and the exact p is below 0.05 in the same direction (with fewer than 100 changed pairs, the exact test governs). First-pick differences and projection accuracy are descriptive.
decisionRule: Classic stays the default in this release whatever the result. If the primary comparison shows a significant loss (as defined in the analysis), the look-ahead is withdrawn from the page and kept only for study; otherwise it ships as an experimental option. It may later be proposed as the default only after a significant primary gain. The owner makes the final call in every case. The result is published either way.
